ai.description: This slender, 20–30 cm snake is uniform pale brown to reddish-tan. It features a distinct, down-curved rostral scale forming a hook-like snout and a terminal spine on the tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Myriopholis macrorhyncha* is best distinguished by its prominent, hooked snout and a single, enlarged preocular scale that contacts both the nasal and ocular scales.
ai.habitat: *Myriopholis macrorhyncha* inhabits arid and semi-arid regions, typically found in sandy soils within thorn scrub forests and dry grasslands at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The hook-snouted worm snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its time burrowing through loose soil to forage for ant and termite larvae.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Myriopholis macrorhyncha* is oviparous, typically laying a small clutch of 2–4 elongated eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, usually between July and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Myriopholis macrorhyncha* occurs in arid regions of northwestern India, specifically Rajasthan and Gujarat, typically at low elevations.
